parsed.paper_uuid: Gary Habermas - Chapter 010 - What Scholars Believe About Jesus' Resurrection (Pt. 1) - Gary Habermas

source_selection.exact_source_expression: For something to be a minimal fact, it must have strong evidence and most experts must agree on it.
source_selection.reason: This is a definitional claim about a two-place predicate (minimal fact) over propositions and scholar populations. It is the load-bearing definition for the entire minimal-facts methodology and can be encoded as a definition plus a theorem about the conjunctive structure.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: A proposition P is a minimal fact relative to an evidence relation E and a scholar population S iff P is highly evidenced by E and a vast majority of S concurs that P.

symbol_table.formal_definition: IsMinimalFact E S P := HighlyEvidenced E P ∧ VastMajorityConcurs S P
symbol_table.reader_meaning: A historical claim that meets both an evidential bar and a scholarly-consensus bar.
There is strong evidence for P.

symbol_table.formal_definition: VastMajorityConcurs S P := ∀ s ∈ S, Concurs s P
symbol_table.reader_meaning: Most qualified scholars agree that P.

explicit_premises: E is a predicate on propositions representing 'has strong evidence'.
S is a finite or infinite set of scholars.
Concurs is a predicate relating a scholar to a proposition.
assumptions_and_dependencies.theological_starting_premises: None. The definition is neutral with respect to whether any minimal fact is true.
assumptions_and_dependencies.non_vacuity_requirement: There must exist at least one P, E, S such that IsMinimalFact E S P holds; otherwise the definition is vacuous.

verification_controls.interpretation: Lean corpus was not searched and no build was attempted in this run.
No witness for IsMinimalFact was constructed.

result_and_boundary.what_is_established: A precise Lean 4 definition of the minimal-fact predicate as a conjunction of an evidential condition and a consensus condition.
result_and_boundary.what_remains_open: Whether any actual historical proposition satisfies the definition; the definition does not assert existence of minimal facts.
result_and_boundary.encoding_fidelity_review: The source uses 'strong evidence' and 'most experts must agree'; the formalization abstracts these into predicates E and Concurs. The threshold for 'most' is left as a parameter, matching Habermas's refusal to give a numerical threshold (A03).
result_and_boundary.interpretive_connections: Connects to A02 (criterion 1 more important than criterion 2) and A06 (consensus alone insufficient).

source_selection.exact_source_expression: Having strong evidence matters much more than having a majority of scholars agree.
source_selection.reason: This is a comparative priority claim between the two criteria. It can be encoded as a theorem about a weighting function or a lexicographic order on the two criteria.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: For any two minimal-fact candidates P and Q, if P is highly evidenced and Q is not, then P is rationally preferable to Q regardless of the consensus levels of P and Q.

symbol_table.formal_definition: Preferable E S P Q := HighlyEvidenced E P ∧ ¬ HighlyEvidenced E Q
symbol_table.reader_meaning: P is a better candidate for rational belief than Q.
The vast majority of qualified scholars concur.

explicit_premises: Preferable is defined as a relation that ignores consensus when evidence differs.
The domain of propositions is nonempty.
assumptions_and_dependencies.non_vacuity_requirement: There must exist at least two propositions P and Q with differing evidence status.

verification_controls.interpretation: No countermodel was constructed to test whether the priority claim is consistent with the definition.

result_and_boundary.what_is_established: A formal statement of the priority of evidence over consensus, conditional on the definition of Preferable.
result_and_boundary.what_remains_open: Whether the priority claim is normatively correct; the theorem only encodes the stated priority, it does not justify it.
result_and_boundary.encoding_fidelity_review: The source says criterion 1 is 'by far the more important' and '90 or 85% of the game' (S329). The formalization captures the qualitative priority but not the quantitative weighting.
result_and_boundary.interpretive_connections: Connects to A06 (consensus alone insufficient) and A01 (definition of minimal fact).

source_selection.exact_source_expression: Just because most scholars agree doesn't mean you should believe it; you also need strong evidence.
source_selection.reason: This is a sufficiency claim: consensus alone is not sufficient for rational belief. It can be encoded as a theorem that VastMajorityConcurs does not imply RationalBelief without HighlyEvidenced.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: There exists a proposition P and scholar population S such that VastMajorityConcurs S P holds but RationalBelief P does not hold, because HighlyEvidenced E P fails.

symbol_table.formal_definition: RationalBelief E S P := HighlyEvidenced E P ∧ VastMajorityConcurs S P
symbol_table.reader_meaning: One is rationally justified in believing P.

explicit_premises: RationalBelief is defined as the conjunction of the two criteria.
There exists at least one proposition with consensus but no evidence.
assumptions_and_dependencies.non_vacuity_requirement: The existential claim requires a witness; without a concrete P the theorem is conditional.

verification_controls.interpretation: No model was constructed to test the claim.

result_and_boundary.what_is_established: A formal statement that consensus alone does not entail rational belief under Habermas's definition.
result_and_boundary.what_remains_open: Whether the definition of RationalBelief is the correct one; the theorem is relative to that definition.
result_and_boundary.encoding_fidelity_review: The source explicitly says 'it's the latter' (S385), meaning both criteria are needed. The formalization matches this.

source_selection.exact_source_expression: Gary doesn't say you need a certain percentage of evidence; he looks for things like many sources, eyewitnesses, and early accounts.
source_selection.reason: This is a claim about the absence of a numerical threshold and the presence of qualitative criteria. It can be encoded as a definition of an evidence profile with no numeric threshold.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: An evidence profile for a proposition P is a tuple of qualitative criteria (multiple attestation, eyewitness testimony, early accounts) with no numerical threshold.

symbol_table.formal_definition: MultipleAttestation P := ∃ n ≥ 2, AttestedBy P n
symbol_table.reader_meaning: P is attested by multiple independent sources.

symbol_table.formal_definition: Eyewitness P := ∃ w, Witness w P
symbol_table.reader_meaning: There is an eyewitness to P.

symbol_table.formal_definition: EarlyAccount P := ∃ c, Creed c ∧ Contains c P
symbol_table.reader_meaning: P appears in an early creed or account.

explicit_premises: AttestedBy, Witness, and Contains are predicates.
assumptions_and_dependencies.non_vacuity_requirement: There must exist at least one proposition with a nonempty evidence profile.

result_and_boundary.what_is_established: A formal definition of an evidence profile using qualitative criteria rather than a percentage.
result_and_boundary.what_remains_open: How to aggregate the criteria into a single 'highly evidenced' predicate; the source does not specify a combination rule.
result_and_boundary.encoding_fidelity_review: The source says 'I don't have a certain threshold' (S206) and lists categories (S226-S228). The formalization captures the categories but leaves the aggregation open.

source_selection.exact_source_expression: Gary says he can choose to use only French, German, and English sources because he's the author, and those are the main languages for research.
source_selection.reason: This is a claim about authorial rights and language restriction. It can be encoded as a definition of a restricted scholar population and a theorem that the restriction is permissible by authorial fiat.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: A language-restricted scholar population S_L is the subset of scholars who publish in languages L. The author may choose L = {French, German, English}.

symbol_table.formal_definition: LanguageRestrictedPopulation L := { s | PublishesIn s l ∧ l ∈ L }
symbol_table.reader_meaning: The set of scholars who publish in the selected languages.
The author is entitled to set the language parameters.

explicit_premises: PublishesIn is a predicate relating scholars to languages.
L is a finite set of languages.
assumptions_and_dependencies.non_vacuity_requirement: There must exist at least one scholar publishing in each of the selected languages.

result_and_boundary.what_is_established: A formal definition of a language-restricted scholar population.
result_and_boundary.what_remains_open: Whether the restriction is epistemically justified; the formalization only encodes the author's stated right, not its normative validity.
result_and_boundary.encoding_fidelity_review: The source says 'I'm the author... that's my right' (S659-S661). The formalization treats AuthorialRight as an uninterpreted predicate.

parsed.notes: The Lean corpus was not searched in this run. All verification controls are NOT_RUN and all verification statuses are CANDIDATE or NOT_ATTEMPTED. The formal candidates are limited to the five strongest mathematically or formally relevant claims. Claims A07-A24 are primarily bibliographic, biographical, or rhetorical and are not formalized here.
